You are given an attached CSV file b3_supercon_data.csv: 300 real samples,
column `composition` (element fractions as a compact formula string) and
column `target` (the measured critical temperature Tc (K)).

Propose a composition — a value for each element fraction below, within each
observed range, that MAXIMIZES critical temperature Tc (K) AND stays robust
— its critical temperature Tc (K) must not collapse under a ±5% change in
any single variable (seek a broad optimum, not a sharp peak). Design
variables:
  - O (fraction in [0, 0.697674])
  - Cu (fraction in [0, 0.454545])
  - Ba (fraction in [0, 0.333333])

turns.answer_text:
**My recommendation is a Y–Ba–Cu–O composition near YBa₂Cu₃O₆.₉₅, as a robustness-oriented candidate—not a proven robust global maximum.** The supplied data do not establish a composition whose Tc is guaranteed to survive every requested ±5% perturbation.

### Evidence from the supplied data

The highest measured Tc using only the permitted elements is **126 K for `Ba2Ca2Cu3O`**. However, this is an isolated observation: there is no nearby Ba–Ca–Cu–O series demonstrating a broad optimum. Also, its recorded oxygen coefficient is 1; interpreting it as an oxygen-rich formula would change the supplied data.

The **YBa₂Cu₃Oₓ region has much stronger repeated support**:

| Recorded composition | Measured Tc (K) |
|---|---:|
| Y1Ba2Cu3O6.82 | 89.9 |
| Y1Ba2Cu3O6.85 | 84.4 |
| Y1Ba2Cu3O6.87 | 93.5 |
| Y1Ba2Cu3O6.95 | 92.8 |
| Y1Ba2Cu3O6.96 | 92.3 |
| Y1Ba2Cu3O7 | 83.0, 90.2 |

This supports a **high-Tc neighborhood rather than a single exceptional observation**, although it also reveals experimental variability. I would avoid adding Zn, Pr, or other substitutions merely to improve a speculative prediction: several such substitutions in this dataset substantially reduce Tc.

### Robustness limitation

These observations **do not validate the full ±5% requirement**. For example, changing the oxygen coefficient of O₆.₉₅ by ±5% gives approximately O₆.₆₀–O₇.₃₀, extending beyond the demonstrated high-Tc neighborhood. Independent ±5% changes in Y, Ba, and Cu likewise lack adequate local coverage. Therefore, **roughly 90 K is an empirical nominal expectation, not a guaranteed perturbed Tc**.

For a physically meaningful test, perturb one nonzero fraction at a time and renormalize all fractions to sum to one. Testing robustness to contamination of zero-valued elements would require a separate, absolute perturbation rule.
